The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1962 prints the conclusion written out (14 words); the public-domain witnesses abbreviate it to the short cue; 1862 text layer damages 4 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: cordibus -> rtordibus; quesumus domine gratiam -> qusesumus i d mine gr tiam; benignus infunde -> be nignus infftnde; carnalibus -> carn libus; 1922 Mame text layer damages 2 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): cordibus -> (absent from the aligned window); quesumus -> quesu mus; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 116, artifact PDF p. 230; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 30381 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Cordibus nostris, quaesumus, Domine, gratiam tuam benignus infunde: ut,
sicut ab escis carnalibus abstinemus; ita sensus quoque nostros a noxiis
retrahamus excessibus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui
tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

perfice sacramentum. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens et misericors Deus: ut, quod ore contingimus,
pura mente capiamus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui
tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.
